skill.name: api-dev

skill.summary: Build scalable APIs with async patterns, versioning, documentation, tests, rate limits, and production checklists.

security_audit.summary: Most static findings are false positives from Markdown code fences, placeholder URLs, request object names, and Redis URL parameters in examples. One critical issue is confirmed: the caching example deserializes Redis data with pickle.loads, which can enable code execution if cache data is controlled or poisoned. No prompt injection or malicious marketplace intent was found.

remediation.issue: Unsafe pickle deserialization in the response cache example.
remediation.suggestion: Replace pickle.loads and pickle.dumps with JSON, MessagePack, or another schema-validating serializer. Do not deserialize untrusted cache data.

remediation.issue: Redis connection parameters appear in reusable examples.
remediation.suggestion: Add guidance to load redis_url from a secret manager or secure configuration. Never hardcode, print, or expose connection strings.

content.value_statement: Teams need consistent patterns for fast, secure APIs. This skill provides reusable async, testing, documentation, caching, and deployment guidance.
actual_capabilities: Explains async API clients with connection pooling and request metrics.
Shows circuit breaker patterns for fault tolerance.
Provides Redis-backed rate limiting middleware examples.
Covers API versioning through headers, paths, and query parameters.
Includes OpenAPI response schema and server configuration patterns.
Includes async API test examples and a production checklist.
limitations: The skill provides examples, not a runnable package.
Python examples are most detailed, so other languages need adaptation.
Security examples require review before production use.
The cache example uses pickle and should be replaced before use.

use_cases.title: Design a New API Service
use_cases.description: Plan endpoints, versioning, error responses, and documentation before implementation starts.

use_cases.title: Standardize Platform API Patterns
use_cases.description: Create shared guidance for rate limits, caching, monitoring, and production configuration.

use_cases.title: Build API Test Coverage
use_cases.description: Draft async unit, integration, pagination, and rate limit tests for service workflows.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a Basic REST API
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to design a REST API for a small service. Include endpoints, status codes, error shapes, and OpenAPI notes.

prompt_templates.title: Review API Middleware
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to review my API middleware plan for authentication, validation, logging, rate limiting, and error handling.

prompt_templates.title: Improve Async Performance
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to improve an async API client. Focus on connection pooling, timeouts, circuit breakers, caching, and observability.

prompt_templates.title: Audit Production Readiness
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to audit my API for production readiness. Cover security headers, versioning, tests, monitoring, cache safety, and rollback risks.

output_examples.input: I need a user profile API for a mobile app.
output: A versioned endpoint plan for create, read, update, and delete operations.
A standard error response model with validation and authorization cases.
OpenAPI documentation notes for pagination, authentication, and rate limits.

output_examples.input: My API slows down when external services fail.
output: A circuit breaker strategy with failure thresholds and reset timing.
Timeout, retry, and connection pool recommendations for async calls.
Metrics to track latency, error rate, and dependency health.

output_examples.input: I need tests for a new API workflow.
output: A focused async test plan for create, read, update, and delete flows.
Checks for pagination, hidden password fields, and rate limiting behavior.
Mocking guidance for external services and integration boundaries.

best_practices: Adapt examples to your framework and verify security before deployment.
Use explicit timeouts, connection limits, and structured error responses.
Document versioning, rate limits, authentication, and deprecation rules.
anti_patterns: Do not copy cache serialization examples without replacing unsafe pickle usage.
Do not expose credentials or connection strings in logs, docs, or examples.
Do not rely on tests alone without production monitoring and dependency health checks.

faq.question: Does this skill generate a complete API project?
faq.answer: No. It provides patterns and examples that you adapt to your existing framework.

faq.question: Which languages does it support best?
faq.answer: The examples focus on Python, but the architecture guidance applies to Node.js, Go, and similar stacks.

faq.question: Can I use it with Claude, Codex, and Claude Code?
faq.answer: Yes. The report lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: Does it cover API documentation?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes OpenAPI configuration patterns, response schemas, and documentation checklist items.

faq.question: Does it include security guidance?
faq.answer: Yes. It discusses authentication, authorization, validation, headers, rate limiting, and production review points.

faq.question: Is every code example safe for production?
faq.answer: No. Review and harden each example, especially the cache serialization pattern that uses pickle.
